notes.title: ⚡️ Flow Trigger
notes.text:
A trigger initiates the flow. It can be a built-in tool or an integration with an external application.
Trigger Types:
1. 📱App - Initiate flow from an external application integration
2. 🔌 Interface - API / Webhook
3. 💬 Widget - Prebuilt UI component (Chat, Search)
📖 Read Docs - Flows

notes.title: ➕ Nodes
notes.text:
Nodes are the fundamental building blocks of a flow. Each node serves a specific purpose, acting as a self-contained unit that processes input and produces output. This modular approach allows users to create complex flows by interconnecting various nodes.
Node Types:
1. 📱 Apps - Integrate third-party applications into your flow.
2. 🤖 AI - Perform AI operations within your flow.
3. 🛢️ Data - Manipulate and transform data within your flow.
4. ♾️ Logic - Control the flow of execution in your flow.

notes.title: 💬 Flow response
notes.text: The final step of your flow can send output to an external system, which is particularly useful for flows initiated by triggers like Chat or GraphQL API integrations.

notes.title: ▶️ Try it out
notes.text:
1. Chat Widget trigger allows you to run a flow whenever a user sends a message.
🎨 Customize Chat Widget appearance and behaviour inside the chat widget node.
2. 🛠️ Configure AI Node for text Generation
AI Nodes allow you to generate content and reasoning with LLMs.
  ⚙️ Setup Model
  ✍🏻 Configure Prompt
  ▶️ Test AI Node
3. ➕ Map the output to the chat response
4. Run flow by clicking ▶️ Test 👇🏻
5. Find Setup instructions to embed this widget on your website: 〈〉 Setup 👆🏻
